title: GovernanceCertification predicate v1
description: An in-toto predicate (predicateType https://loomground.org/attestations/GovernanceCertification/v1). It rides a DSSE-signed in-toto Statement whose `subject` is the governed action (name + sha256 digest of the action envelope). It asserts that, AT THE MOMENT IT ACTED, a specific AI action was simultaneously grounded AND overseen AND enforced AND intact AND legitimate. The `enforced` pillar is load-bearing: this predicate is only issuable because the action passed through a runtime gate that would OTHERWISE have blocked it. Possessing a valid, signed instance is therefore evidence the governance happened, not a claim that it did. Everything mechanical is composed: DSSE + in-toto (envelope/transport), Ed25519 + RFC 8785 (signing/canonicalisation), the grounding SCHEME (5d+nd / prov-o / uri-span — pluggable). The ONLY thing this schema owns is the shape of the five pillars.

verdict.description: The governed outcome that PRODUCED this certification. A `deny` produces no certification (there was nothing to certify but a refusal); only these two outcomes mint one.

action_class.description: The action's governed class (e.g. shell.exec, fs.write, mcp.<server>.<tool>). The full action body is the in-toto Statement `subject`, digest-bound.

issued_at.description: RFC 3339 UTC timestamp the certification was minted (at gate time).

enforced.description: THE load-bearing pillar. Attests the action was blocked-unless-permitted at runtime — not merely evaluated. Without this being true and mechanism-named, the artifact is a claim, not proof.

mechanism.description: The gate that would have blocked the action (e.g. 'claude-code:PreToolUse', 'resource-server:web-bot-auth'). Names WHERE enforcement bit.

blocked_unless_permitted.description: MUST be true. A certification whose gate could not actually block is not enforcement-bound and must not be issued.

decision_ref.description: Identifier of the gate decision (the chokepoint's audit id) this certification was minted from.

overseen.description: The human-oversight pillar — an oversight-certificate (its own repo; already DSSE, so it embeds as an in-toto-compatible sub-attestation). For verdict `permit` a human step may be absent (grade permitted it); for `hold-approved` it MUST be present.

required.description: Whether a human oversight step was required for this action.

disposition.description: The oversight-certificate disposition when a human acted. Refuse-to-decide (ABSTAINED) is first-class.

qualifier.description: Identifier/role of the qualified human, as attested by the oversight-certificate (never raw PII — a stable pseudonymous id).

oversight_certificate.description: The embedded oversight-certificate DSSE envelope, OR a digest reference to it. Re-checkable offline from its own public key.

grounded.description: The provenance pillar — the verdict rests on a cited span, addressed in a PLUGGABLE scheme. `scheme` is a URI (5d+nd / prov-o / uri-span / 7d+nd …); `digest` lets any verifier re-check without understanding the scheme; `evidence` optionally inlines the resolved span for cross-boundary verification. Ungrounded (absent ref) is not certifiable.

scheme.description: URI naming the grounding scheme. The certification does not privilege any one; a verifier resolves it via whatever understands that vocabulary.

ref.description: The scheme-specific span/coordinate. Opaque to the certification (like an in-toto subject name).

digest.description: {algorithm: value}, e.g. {"sha256": "…"} over the canonicalised (RFC 8785) ref. Re-checkable without the scheme resolver.

evidence.description: Optional inline copy of the resolved span (the VC `evidence` pattern) so a verifier WITHOUT store access can still re-check the digest.

intact.description: The integrity pillar — the decision is recorded on a tamper-evident append-only log, linked so a verifier can confirm inclusion + linearity. REUSE-FIRST: prefer an existing transparency-log inclusion proof (Sigstore Rekor, or an RFC 6962 / RFC 9162 Merkle proof) so off-the-shelf verifiers apply; fall back to RVND's native per-folder Ed25519 hash chain only where no log is deployed. `type` names which.

type.description: The integrity mechanism, reuse-first. 'rekor' / 'rfc6962' carry a standard inclusion proof; 'native-chain' is RVND's own hash chain.

entry_ref.description: Log index / event id for this decision.

inclusion_proof.description: The standard proof when type is rekor/rfc6962 (Merkle inclusion). Absent for native-chain.

prev_hash.description: Previous event hash — linearity check for native-chain.

legitimate.description: The policy-legitimacy pillar — the policy the verdict was evaluated against is itself anchored to real sources (span-norms into instruments), not an ad-hoc rule. `anchors` cite where the governing rules rest.

policy_fingerprint.description: Digest of the effective policy the verdict used (matrix + oversight row + posture).

anchors.description: The span-norm/source anchors the governing rules rest on (e.g. instrument + pinpoint, or a grounding ref). May reuse the `grounded` scheme.
